A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WDPO/KLDPO research. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H can be matched reliably; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: V2 reports original GPT-2 Emotion alignment and LLaMA alignment experiments, including ArmoRM evaluations, leaderboard scores, and additional results in Appendices E-F.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and appendix results, with revisions to the main leaderboard summary.

M1.justification: The WDPO gradient regularization and KLDPO loss reweighting procedures remain unchanged in Algorithms 1-2. Appendix F retains the same implementation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use Emotion alignment, HelpSteer2/ArmoRM alignment, and the same OpenLLM Leaderboard tasks. The emotion mixtures, unseen reward objectives, and appendix evaluation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: V3 removes the SFT LLaMA-3.2-1B-Instruct baseline from Table 1. DPO and its epoch variants remain, and no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: The reported preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The additional 1B configurations summarized in v3 Table 1 were already evaluated in v2 Appendix Table 3.

E4.justification: Both retain the convex and geometric emotion shifts, unseen ArmoRM objective evaluations, appendix reward-mixture tests, and DPO epoch comparisons. No distinct ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3's checklist marks statistical significance as not applicable but introduces no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes several 1B aggregates: DPO epoch-2 GPQA rises from 0.26 to 0.27, while WDPO with rho_o = 0.01 has MATH revised from 0.10 to 0.09. It removes SFT results and adds aggregates for configurations already in Table 3. The 3B/8B scores, appendix subtask scores, and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, mathematical definitions, estimation-error bounds, worst-case distribution characterization, and proofs in Appendices A-D remain unchanged. Apparent extraction differences in mathematical symbols are typesetting differences.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about distributionally robust DPO, policy-parameter guarantees, tractable algorithms, and robustness to preference shifts.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 removes the interpretation that DPO underperforms SFT even with early stopping and that this highlights the need for robust methods. Other result interpretations and Appendix G's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new checklist promises open data and code upon acceptance and documentation alongside code release. These are additional release statements, not evidence of actual availability. The existing repository link and Appendix F's technical details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds distributionally robust imitation learning through Bashiri et al. (2021) and Panaganti et al. (2023), plus robust offline learning through Panaganti et al. (2025). The principal novelty positioning is retained; several other references receive publication metadata updates.

P1.justification: The scientific narrative remains largely verbatim. V3 adds a NeurIPS checklist, updates affiliation and contact information, makes local wording edits, and removes the separate Section 6.1 heading while retaining its content.

P2.justification: V3 reformats the document throughout into the denser NeurIPS layout, places Algorithms 1-2 side by side, consolidates Table 1's two 1B panels, and groups appendix Tables 3-4 together. Existing figures are resized and relocated, with their graphical content retained.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves conflicting duplicate 1B entries and brings Table 1's aggregates into agreement with the retained appendix scores, modestly improving the accuracy and coherence of the central comparison. Removing the SFT baseline reduces context about performance relative to the starting model, limiting the gain. The underlying methods, theory, and experiments remain unchanged.
